title: Light Speed Stop 11: The Milky Way
topic: Light-speed journey stop 11: the Milky Way (~100,000 light-years across; ~100-400 billion stars; most stars have planets; Sun ~26,000 light-years from center; orbit ~230 million years; Sagittarius A* ~4 million Suns)
links_to_previous: Answers episode 10's cliffhanger (more planets than stars?): yes, on average at least one planet per star. The journey continues across the Milky Way.
cliffhanger_question: Is the Milky Way on a collision course with another galaxy? Yes or no?
summary: Answer: yes, astronomers estimate most stars have at least one planet. The Milky Way is about 100,000 light-years across with hundreds of billions of stars and a black hole at its heart. Next stop: our neighbor Andromeda.

visual.query: exoplanets Kepler artist concept many planets

scenes.narration: Astronomers estimate most stars have at least one planet.
Now we leave Proxima and zoom out to our home galaxy.
It's about one hundred thousand light-years across.

visual.query: Milky Way galaxy structure artist concept

scenes.narration: Light takes a hundred thousand years just to cross it.
It holds somewhere between one hundred and four hundred billion stars.
We live in a quiet spiral arm, about twenty-six thousand light-years from the center.
The Sun circles the center once every two hundred and thirty million years.
At the center sits a black hole, about four million times the Sun's mass.

visual.query: Sagittarius A* black hole Event Horizon Telescope

scenes.narration: In twenty twenty-two, we finally photographed it.

visual.query: Sagittarius A* black hole image Event Horizon Telescope

scenes.narration: And the Milky Way has a giant neighbor, the Andromeda galaxy.
Next stop, Andromeda. Is it on a collision course with us? Yes or no?
